subject_entity.notes: Minutes of the Council of Carthage held September 1, 256 under Cyprian's presidency; 87 bishops from North Africa each individually voted that heretical baptism is invalid and converts must be rebaptized; the fullest extant record of North African episcopal collegial practice; each bishop's sententium preserved verbatim; opposed by Pope Stephen I and eventually overturned by later church practice accepting heretical baptism.

object_entity.notes: Bishop of Carthage c. 248–258; major Latin theologian of ecclesiology and sacramental theology; converted c. 246; deeply influenced by Tertullian; key figure in the Novatian controversy (supported Cornelius against Novatian); martyred under Valerian.

evidence.notes: Cyprian presides and speaks in the Sententiae.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Cyprian said: You have heard, most beloved colleagues, what Jubaianus our fellow bishop wrote to me, consulting my moderate ability about the unlawful and profane baptism of heretics, and what I wrote back to him. Let each of us now bring forward what we think on this matter, judging no man nor rejecting any from the right of communion if he should think differently from us. For none of us sets himself up as a bishop of bishops or by tyrannical terror forces his colleagues to obedience.
passage.notes: Episcopal collegiality; no bishop of bishops; conciliar freedom of conscience

object_entity.proposition_label: Baptism administered by heretics or schismatics is invalid and must be repeated
object_entity.description: Baptism conferred outside the one Church by heretics or schismatics is no baptism at all; converts from heretical groups must be baptized anew because the Holy Spirit operates only within the Church. Held by Cyprian and the African councils; opposed by Stephen of Rome who accepted heretical baptism if in trinitarian form.

evidence.notes: Caecilius of Biltha: one baptism in the Church, none outside.
